description: Two sections in 2HP each reporting whether a signal is rising, flat or falling, as gates or as triggers

params.text: Sets how big a change between readings counts as movement: 0V fully counter-clockwise, 0.0005V at the centre and 0.01V fully clockwise, despite the manual naming a different range
Chooses what that output carries: green for a gate held while that phase lasts, red for a 1ms trigger when the phase begins

inputs.text: The signal that section measures; with the B jack empty the B section reads the A signal

outputs.text: Carries a gate while that section is rising, or a trigger as the rise begins
Carries a gate while that section is flat, or a trigger as the steady phase begins
Carries a gate while that section is falling, or a trigger as the fall begins

notes: a phase lasts until a different one begins, so short flat patches do not interrupt a rise; a steady phase needs the whole hold time flat, 6ms unless you change it
this module is monophonic; a polyphonic input is read on channel 1 only
feeding a slow source that updates only every 64th or 256th cycle makes each step between readings large, so the threshold usually has to be raised for a steady phase to be recognised at all
the red light above the threshold knob means a timing setting is shorter than one process interval and cannot be kept to; its tooltip names which one
menu: Input smoothing — smooths each section's input before the slope is measured, with time constants from 0.5ms to 100ms, and is Off unless you set it
Slope reversal hysteresis: Off (1x, default), 1.5x, 2x, 3x, 5x — makes an already running rise or fall harder to reverse, by requiring that many times the threshold in the other direction
Steady hold time — sets how long the signal must stay flat before the steady phase starts, from Off through 1ms up to 10 seconds, and 6ms unless you change it
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Gate-high output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while high, 10V unless you change it
Gate-low output-level — sets the voltage a gate output carries while low, 0V unless you change it
Trigger-high output-level — sets the voltage a trigger pulse carries during its 1ms high phase, 10V unless you change it
Trigger-low output-level — sets the voltage a trigger output carries between pulses, 0V unless you change it

inputs.0:
one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
one channel only

unpatched it reads the A-CV input.
